question: Should Discord component callbacks default to 7 days and allow a 30-day `agentComponents.ttlMs` ceiling for existing deployments?
rationale: The patch is mechanically small, but it changes how long old visible Discord controls can trigger authorized callback work for users who did not opt into a longer TTL.

options.title: Accept the longer window after blocker fixes
options.body: Land the 7-day default and 30-day maximum after the config reference and conflict are fixed, accepting the longer authorized stale-action window as the desired Discord behavior.

options.title: Keep short default, allow opt-in longer TTL
options.body: Preserve the 30-minute default and solve async workflows through explicit per-deployment `agentComponents.ttlMs` configuration.

options.title: Choose a narrower bound
options.body: Revise the default or maximum to a shorter maintainer-approved window before merge.

recommendation.title: Accept the longer window after blocker fixes
recommendation.body: Land the 7-day default and 30-day maximum after the config reference and conflict are fixed, accepting the longer authorized stale-action window as the desired Discord behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the prior TTL configuration PR and refreshed the generated config metadata, so they are the best available owner for deciding whether this follow-up default/cap policy should ship.
